newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Mahathir, ex-rival join in bid to take Malaysian state.
newsitem.headline: Mahathir, ex-rival join in bid to take Malaysian state.

text.p: Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, enjoying full party backing for re-election next week, on Thursday launched a bid to recapture Malaysia's sole opposition state with the help of a former rival.
"Independence without any development, happiness and benefit is independence we can do without," Mahathir told a rally of 30,000 people in Kelantan, the poorest of Malaysia's 13 states.
By his side was Prince Razaleigh Hamzah, a revered Kelantan politician and once-bitter enemy who recently defected to the prime minister's United Malays National Organisation (UMNO).
The fundamentalist Parti Islam Se-Malaysia (PAS) will control Kelantan until the country's next general elections in 2000.
But political analysts said Mahathir had already launched his campaign to regain the state with Thursday's rally.
"Five years is a long time to wait for another general election," said a Kuala Lumpur-based political analyst.
"Razaleigh could use his popularity and influence effectively to break up PAS in Kelantan even before the year 2000. After that Kelantan is entirely the federal goverment's," added the analyst.
Mahathir got a warm response at the rally. Kelantan men, old and young, children and women braved a hot afternoon to listen to the premier try to persuade them to forget PAS.

UMNO is the linchpin of the ruling National Front coalition. Razaleigh was a senior official in the party and a minister in Mahathir's cabinet until he challenged the premier for the top UMNO post in 1987.
The Kelantan prince lost narrowly and left UMNO, taking a horde of supporters to form the opposition Spirit of 46.

Razaleigh's party then supported PAS in the 1990 general elections to win Kelantan and rule the state together. But the liberal ways of Razaleigh and the rigid, fundamentalist stance of PAS' Kelantan chief Nik Aziz Nik Mat made it difficult for the two to keep the pact, analysts said.
They said Razaleigh's defection and the return of the Spirit of 46 to UMNO was a major victory for Mahathir ahead of UMNO's triennial elections next week, analysts said.
Mahathir has been assured that his post, and that of his deputy, would not be contested in the party elections.
